provenance_note: Pinned source snapshot for three catalogue-listed main results. All three selected theorem targets passed Lemqo's statement binding and independent Nanoda checking; see verification/ and docs/openai.md for exact scope and trust assumptions.

candidates.title: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph
candidates.main_result: There is an absolute constant C > 0 such that every finite simple graph on n vertices has an edge-disjoint partition into cycles and single edges using at most C n pieces. The formalized statement includes edgeless and small graphs; it does not determine the optimal C.

candidates.title: A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
candidates.main_result: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex whose number of out-neighbors at directed distance exactly two is at least its outdegree. The scope excludes the starting vertex and first out-neighbors from the second neighborhood, and includes sinks.

candidates.title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk’s covering assertion
candidates.main_result: The main comparator target states that the compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in R^4 lies in the trace-one symmetric matrix space, has diameter sqrt(2), and cannot be covered by ten arbitrary subsets of strictly smaller diameter. The solution module separately derives an isometric image in R^9 giving the nine-dimensional Euclidean counterexample; that corollary is not among this comparator’s named theorem targets.
